The patient presents with painful vision loss, choroidal detachments, and posterior scleral enhancement on MRI, which are all consistent with posterior scleritis. Additionally, the presence of vitreous cells and the resolution of choroidal detachments with treatment support this diagnosis.

The patient has subretinal fluid, retinal detachment, and late leakage on fluorescein angiography, which are all characteristic of serous retinal detachment. However, the presence of painful vision loss and choroidal detachments suggests that posterior scleritis may be the underlying cause of the serous retinal detachment.
